historical_claims.anchor: The book is famously difficult to place on a conventional timeline.
Heller published Catch-22 in 1961, long after the wartime setting.
He had flown missions as a bombardier in the United States Army Air Forces.
Brandeis University preserves manuscripts and correspondence that show Heller's long process of revision; the published novel was not an immediate reaction to one news cycle.
Heller learned from writers such as Louis-Ferdinand Celine, whose work he discussed in connection with the invention of his own voice.
